meta.title: Ondra Installer
meta.description: A manifest-driven installer: a nine-step pipeline, an independent hash per component, one verification before writing and one after, a ledger in the user's home, and a completeness self-check at the end. The handbook names the old project's disease precisely: a manifest with hashes but no ledger and no self-check command, and those three are this package's backbone. Order matters: verification is hard-ordered before writing, so a failed hash writes not a single byte; the other way round leaves the target directory dirty, and rolling back means either deleting something the user cannot get back or keeping a broken file that explodes further away on the next start. Overwriting gets its own step: a path present in the ledger was installed by us and may be upgraded, while a same-named file the ledger does not know about belongs to someone else and is refused by default. The ledger is written in two phases, half-installed first and installed second, so a process killed mid-copy leaves a clear need-to-reinstall instead of a silent never-installed. It rehearses by default because installation is the only capability that writes into the user's directories. All paths default to empty and report a missing manifest, source or destination instead of guessing, since a guessed destination grows a runtime tree out of nowhere. Failures never roll back automatically, that belongs to the snapshot plugin, and archives are reported unsupported rather than pretended to unpack, because no dependency may be installed here.
